newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen higher ahead of Telekom float.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen higher ahead of Telekom float.

text.p: The German DAX of 30 leading shares was expected to continue to rally on Friday and aim for the crucial level of 2,800 points ahead of the flotation of Deutsche Telekom next week, dealers said.

The IBIS DAX, which measures computer dealings in the blue-chip DAX index, was up 14.60 points, or 0.53 percent, at 2,785.21 points, having touched an intraday record high of 2,789.94 in pre-bourse trade.
Computer dealings were encouraged by a firmer dollar against the mark, German bond strength and a slightly stronger opening on Wall Street.
Dealers were unsure what effect the expiry on Friday of certain share and DAX options would have on price levels, but most expected the DAX to tackle 2,800 points.

Thursday's best performer was Commerzbank which ended IBIS dealings up 1.4 marks, or almost four percent at 36.65 marks, having jumped over five percent in heavy volumes in pre-bourse dealings on merger talk in the market.
The whole banking sector was buoyed by merger fever, Dresdner Bank rising over three percent or 1.38 marks to 44.58 points, while Deutsche Bank was up over two percent or 1.66 marks to 72.11 marks.

Daimler Benz AG was also heavily traded and hit a year high of 99.70 marks in pre-bourse dealings, but the stock could not penetrate the 100 mark level and later fell back on profit-taking to end down 1.35 marks at 97.75 marks.
Deutsche Lufthansa also ended lower, down 36 pfennigs at 20.16 marks, after the German governmant said it would plan to sell the rest of its 36 percent stake in the airline.
